I can’t open the deck to see slide content, so this is a general recommendation based on a typical 10‑minute investor/customer pitch.

Drop slides 6 (Architecture) and 7 (Security).

Why:
- Both are deep, technical topics that take time to explain but are usually not decisive in a short pitch. You can summarize key architecture points and security assurances in one or two sentences inside “Our approach” or in the Case Study/Team slides if needed.
- For a 10‑minute slot you want to prioritize: Why now, Market size, The Problem, Our Approach, traction/case study, Team and The Ask. Those drive interest and decision-making faster than technical diagrams or detailed security controls.

Alternative (if your audience is highly technical): drop 3 (Market size) and 8 (Pricing) instead — technical audiences care more about design and security than high-level TAM or pricing nuance.

Note: I can’t view the actual slides to tailor this further; if you tell me the audience (investors vs customers vs engineers) I can refine the choice.
